messages:
Ade (support): Heads-up, multiple customers reporting sudden 502/504 spikes for hosted inference in eu-south-az2. Errors started ~10:23UTC and are steady. Customers see auth retries + some billing webhook failures.
Julia (oncall): I can see a spike in gateway 502s and connection resets from the LB to the egress hosts. Alert: `gateway.502.rate > 10r/m` for eu-south-az2.
Aj (infra): Is this only auth routes or all endpoints?
Ade (support): Mostly /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Some customers reported tokens failing with 5xx on initial handshake, then successful on retry. Example from customer curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.com (34.x.x.x) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-request-id: 01F8ABCXY1234
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.com left intact
```
Customer also provided a tcpdump showing retransmits and some RSTs between LB and egress host.
Mike (sre): I see matching traces: increased retransmit counts and path MTU messages around the same time. Looks like packet fragmentation/retransmit bursts.
infra-bot: [ALERT] provider-peering: BGP flaps detected to ISP-AS58432 from eu-south-pop-3 at 10:22:46 UTC. Event id: pr-98321
Aj (infra): Provider peering showing route churn to a subset of egress IPs. Could be asymmetric path causing PMTU/fragmentation. I’m opening escal on provider.
Julia (oncall): For mitigation: 1) add a temporary route pinning to eu-south-az1 egress pool for prod hosts; 2) enable fallback region routing for affected customers; 3) increase LB retry window. Thoughts? :eyes:
Mike (sre): Agree. Also throttle large requests that trigger fragmentation (long TLS records?) and force TLS record sizing to 16k->8k on egress to avoid fragmentation. I can push that change to the egress NGINX config.
Aj (infra): Provider confirmed a partial fiber flap causing microburst packet loss and ECN marking. They’re rerouting but ETA 25-40min. Suggest we shift traffic away from their peering for now.
Ade (support): Customers are asking for repro steps. What should I tell them?
Mike (sre): Tell them it's a regional networking issue on our ISP peering to eu-south-az2 causing packet loss between LB and egress nodes which results in 502s/timeouts on first attempt; retries typically succeed. Workaround: retry logic client-side or switch region. Example repro: run repeated curl in quick succession and watch for intermittent 502s and different x-request-id values: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s %{header_x_request_id}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"a"}'; sleep 0.2; done
```
Julia (oncall): I've applied a quick LB route adjustment to bias away from the affected egress pool. Monitoring.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: `egress-nginx/record-size-fix` -> staging -> canary.
Aj (infra): Provider says BGP settled at 10:46UTC, but we still see some retransmits on the path. Recommend keeping routing bias for another 30m and monitor error rate.
Ade (support): Noted. I'll send a concise customer note: "We observed transient network issues between our edge gateway and a subset of regional egress hosts in eu-south-az2 causing intermittent 502/504 responses. We’ve routed traffic away from the affected path and are monitoring — retries normally succeed and we’re recommending users switch region or implement client retries while we finish remediation."
Mike (sre): Postmortem action items: 1) add automated detection for asymmetric retransmit spikes on LB->egress path; 2) automated regional failover trigger if >X% 5xx over 5m; 3) document TLS record size mitigation and make default; 4) validate provider SLA/route diversity.
Julia (oncall): Error rate dropped from 18r/m to 2r/m after reroute. Keeping this thread open until stable for 2h.
Ade (support): Thanks team. I'll follow up with affected customers with repro snippets and the temporary mitigation. :thumbsup:
